papers.title: Lithium‐Induced Thickness‐Dependent Magnetic Structure Transition in 2D Fe 3 GaTe 2
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The nonvolatile control of magnetic structures in 2D ferromagnets is essential for advancing spintronics. Here, gate‐tunable lithium intercalation is demonstrated as an effective strategy for modulating the magnetic properties of Fe 3 GaTe 2 in a pronounced thickness‐dependent manner. In flakes thicker than 27 nm, partial Li intercalation induces a functional ferromagnetic–antiferromagnetic vertical heterostructure, evidenced by an enhanced coercive field and a giant exchange bias of ∼0.31 T. Conversely, in flakes thinner than 20 nm, full Li penetration leads to a mixed‐phase transition, resulting in reduced coercivity and no exchange bias is observed. Real‐space magnetic force microscopy (MFM) imaging, combined with in situ atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), directly reveals the thickness‐dependent evolution of magnetic domains and lattice distortions, providing a structural basis for the observed modulation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations support these findings, confirming a lithium‐induced ferromagnetic‐to‐antiferromagnetic phase transition accompanied by lattice expansion. These results highlight the exceptional magnetic tunability of Fe 3 GaTe 2 via ionic control and establish gate‐controlled intercalation as a reconfigurable platform for engineering topological spin textures and energy‐efficient magnetic memory devices.

papers.title: Laser Subtracting Multinary Metal Oxides Activates Photoassisted Discharge in Li‐O 2 Battery
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Utilizing photo‐generated carriers to boost charge–discharge process is of significance in photo‐assisted lithium‐oxygen batteries (PLOBs), while this poses a great challenge for low‐cost multinary metal oxides (MMOs) photoelectrodes on the unfavorable conduction band that is generally lower than the reduction potential of Li 2 O 2 to Li. The present work demonstrates a universal strategy of laser subtracting bulk MMOs, yielding gram‐scale MMOs nanocrystals with a favorable band position that allows for photo‐generated electrons to participate in photo‐assisted reduction of oxygen. The extreme conditions manufacturing endows the MMO nanocrystals with unique surface states with abundant Lewis acid‐base sites, which is experimentally verified to be favorable for acceleration of electrochemical reaction kinetics in PLOBs. Exemplified by photoelectrodes comprising laser‐subtracted BiVO 4 (BVO) NCs with elevated conduction band and tailored surface states, which achieve a high discharge potential of 3.25 V and low charge potential of 2.98 V (0.1 mA cm −2 ) with a round‐trip efficiency of 109%, and excellent cycling stability over 255 cycles with only 0.027% capacity decay per cycle, surpassing previously reported metal oxide‐based cathodes in PLOBs. Such a laser‐subtracting strategy was further found to be general in yielding many other MMOs NCs with activated photo‐assisted discharge behaviors, thus paving an efficient way to discover potential bifunctional photoelectrodes for PLOBs based on laser‐matter interactions.

In‐Situ Polymerization MXene@PAF‐1 for Triboelectric Nanogenerators With High Surface Charge Density Toward Self‐Powered Cardiovascular Assessment
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The development of high‐performance triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is fundamentally limited by low surface charge density and rapid charge dissipation in conventional polymer dielectrics. Herein, an in situ polymerization strategy was proposed to construct MXene@PAF‐1, which is further incorporated into a poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) matrix to fabricate triboelectric dielectric films. The intercalated porous aromatic framework (PAF‐1) suppresses MXene restacking and introduces abundant deep‐trap sites, thereby enhancing charge storage and retention. Meanwhile, strong interfacial interactions promote β‐phase crystallization and interfacial polarization, synergistically improving surface charge density. As a result, the MXene@PAF‐1@PVDF based TENG achieves an output voltage of 770 V, current density of 31 mA/m 2 and peak power density of 9.2 W/m 2 , representing an approximately 18‐fold enhancement over pristine PVDF devices. Kelvin probe force microscopy combined with surface potential decay analysis reveals an ∼81.8‐fold increase in deep‐trap density, confirming the critical role of PAF‐1 in charge stabilization. In addition, the device enables self‐powered, high‐fidelity pulse sensing, while convolutional neural network‐assisted analysis allows accurate extraction of cardiovascular parameters and differentiation between healthy and hypertensive subjects. This work provides an effective strategy for trap‐engineered triboelectric dielectrics toward intelligent self‐powered healthcare electronics.

papers.title: Investigation Into the Electrochemical Performance of Micron‐ and Nanosized Tin in Diglyme and Carbonate Electrolytes in Sodium Ion Batteries (Adv. Energy Mater. 27/2026)
papers.abstract_en: Sodium Ion Batteries In article number e71023, John T. S. Irvine and co-workers found that the cycling stability of Sn negative electrode is governed not only by mechanical expansion of Sn but also by the interplay between particle size and electrolyte chemistry. Diglyme electrolytes maintain electrode integrity through a robust SEI despite extreme volume changes, while carbonate electrolytes suffer catalytic decomposition on Sn surfaces, leading to unstable interphases and accelerated capacity fading. These findings reveal that interfacial instability, amplified by particle-size reduction, dominates long-term degradation.

papers.title: High-rate single-crystalline Li-rich layered oxide with diversified surface-phase cation ordering for Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract_en: Advanced lithium-ion batteries require fast-charging high-energy-density electrodes. Li- and Mn-rich layered positive electrodes can offer higher capacity (>280 mAh g−1) and higher specific energy (>1000 Wh kg−1) than Ni-rich chemistries, yet it is challenging to produce volumetric-energy-dense Li-rich single crystals. Another concern is the rate performance. Li-rich layered oxides have long been considered to have poor rate capability, not to mention their single-crystal version. Here we report high-rate single-crystal Li-rich layered oxides with fast rechargeability. 0.2 C-discharge capacity of 248 mAh g−1at 5 C fast-charging as well as 5 C fast-discharging capacity of 179 mAh g−1 are demonstrated. We prove that the fast rechargeability can be resolved by a complex cation ordering of coherent layered-, cation mixed-, rock salt-, and spinel-type structure. The highly conductive and electrochemically active surface phases can buffer Li+ concentration gradients and enable deeper bulk lithiation. The single-crystal morphology and redesigned surface phase ensure mechanical and structural stability over cycling, improving capacity retention to 94.5% over 150 cycles at 0.5 C-rate. This work uncovers the intrinsic high-rate performance of single-crystal Li-rich layered oxides and calls attention to think about the fast-charging potential of positive electrodes with coarse microstructure. Li-rich and single-crystal battery positive electrodes are typically slow to charge/discharge. Here, authors show that single crystal Li- and Mn-rich positive electrodes with a structurally complex surface structure can charge quickly, deliver high capacity, and cycle stably.
papers.summary_ko: 고속 충방전이 가능한 단결정 리튬리치 층상 산화물 양극을 개발했다. 층상-양이온혼합-암염-스피넬이 공존하는 복잡한 양이온 정렬 구조를 통해 5C 고속충전에서 248 mAh/g(0.2C 방전 기준), 5C 방전에서도 179 mAh/g의 용량을 달성해 리튬리치 산화물의 고질적인 낮은 율속 성능 문제를 극복했다.

papers.title: High energy-density, fast-chargeable lithium-ion batteries by mechanically interlocked polymers
papers.abstract_en: Silicon anodes can play a key role in improving the energy density and fast-charging capability of lithium-ion batteries; however, their uncontrolled swelling remains a formidable hurdle in practice, particularly at a high electrode density, an essential parameter for high volumetric energy density. To address this challenge, we report here a polymeric poly(acrylic acid) binder with mechanically interlocked crosslinks to realize a topologically entangled polymer network. This binder system effectively dissipates the stress resulting from electrode calendering and repeated cycling via various mechanical motions at the mechanically interlocked crosslinks, which offer spatially homogeneous mechanical strength and elasticity. This design markedly improves the cycle life and fast-charging capability of silicon-graphite electrodes over those using conventional binders at high electrode densities, highlighting the usefulness of a mechanically interlocked polymer network in distributing the stress of high-capacity battery electrodes during their fabrication and operation.

papers.title: Heterovalent Ion Doping in MOFs for Tailoring Lewis Acidity Toward Synergistic Polysulfide Adsorption and Catalytic Conversion in Li–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The sulfur reduction reaction (SRR) involves complex multi‐phase transitions, posing conflicting demands that single‐component catalysts cannot meet. Zr‐based MOFs (e.g., UiO‐66) offer high stability but suffer from orbital mismatch between hard Lewis acidic nodes and soft polysulfides, limiting host–guest interactions and hindering liquid‐to‐solid conversion kinetics. Herein, we bridge this gap through Lewis acidity tailoring. A Co‐doped UiO‐66‐NO 2 modified separator is constructed to establish a synergistic hard–soft acid interface. By incorporating soft Co active sites into the robust hard Zr‐MOF framework, we harmonize the host–guest interaction based on the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) principle. DFT calculations and kinetic analyses reveal a specific dual‐mechanism where the Co sites utilize optimized d‐p orbital hybridization to strongly anchor soft polysulfides, while concurrently acting as targeted catalytic centers to severely reduce the nucleation barrier of the sluggish Li 2 S 4 → Li 2 S 2 /Li 2 S transformation. Consequently, the cell achieves a high reversible capacity of 902.1 mAh g −1 at 0.5 C and an ultralow decay rate of 0.0238% over 500 cycles. This work not only demonstrates a high‐performance Li–S battery separator but also establishes a molecular‐level HSAB‐guided strategy for designing advanced catalyst materials in multi‐phase conversion electrochemistry.

papers.title: Heteroepitaxial Coating Coupled With Interfacial Electric Field Modulation for Drastically Stabilized Original/Repaired Single‐Crystal Ni‐Rich Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Single crystal Ni‐rich layered cathodes suffer severe capacity fading from interfacial instability and structural deterioration. Herein, a synergistic dual‐coating modification strategy is successfully designed and implemented for single crystal LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 (SC‐NCM622). This strategy comprises an inner coating layer with a heteroepitaxial structure formed by the coherent growth of spinel Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) and layered SC‐NCM622, coupled with an outermost coating layer of Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 /TiO 2 (LTO/TO) composite. The unique dual‐coating effectively suppresses lattice mismatch, oxygen release, structural degradation, and grain cracking, thereby improving Li + reaction kinetics. Concurrently, an interfacial electric field established between LTO and SC‐NCM622 could modulate the inner Helmholtz layer (IHL) through the directional adsorption of PF 6 − anions, thereby forming an inorganic‐rich cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) film. This significantly enhances electrode/electrolyte interface stability and reduces heat generation during cycling. Benefiting from these, the modified sample exhibits exceptional cycling stability, outstanding rate performance, and superior thermal stability at 45°C. In addition, this novel modification strategy has been proven to be equally applicable to the repair and modification of retired SC‐NCM622 cathode materials. This study provides a straightforward and effective approach to address interfacial, kinetic, and thermal stability limitations of single‐crystal Ni‐rich cathodes.

papers.title: Heat‐Activated Micro‐Expansion Hierarchical Coatings for Fire and Grit Impact Resistant Protection of Lithium‐Ion Battery Enclosures
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion battery thermal runaway involves coupled jet flames and particle ejection, posing severe thermo‐mechanical threats to lightweight battery enclosures. Here, a heat‐activated micro‐expansion hierarchical coating is developed to provide durable protection under such extreme conditions. Unlike conventional intumescent or ceramifiable systems, the coating undergoes only moderate volumetric expansion (∼20%) and is observed to form a dual‐phase white‐black barrier after exposure. The flame‐facing surface is characterized by a dense silica‐rich shell that resists flame erosion and particle impact, while the inner region evolves into a porous ceramic‐carbon skeleton that is proposed to contribute to thermal insulation and mechanical buffering. As a result, the coating exhibits markedly reduced heat release in cone calorimetry and sustained protection in the stringent Torch and Grit (TaG) test, maintaining backside temperatures below 250°C for 10 min. Importantly, a real‐time demonstration shows that the battery maintains stable voltage output throughout testing. This work establishes a heat‐activated micro‐expansion hierarchical protection strategy to maintain stable electrical output and circuit continuity under extreme abuse conditions.

papers.title: Harnessing π–d Orbital Hybridization in Non‐Conjugated Linker‐Engineered Iron‐Tetrapyrrole Frameworks to Boost Oxygen Reduction
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Well‐defined Fe–N 4 molecular catalysts offer an ideal platform for probing oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalytic fundamentals, yet their rational molecular design remains challenging. More critically, the role and tunability of π–d orbital hybridization, a key electronic interaction between the Fe center and its organic matrix, are poorly understood, hindering electronic‐level catalyst optimization. To address these issues, we introduce a nonconjugated linker engineering strategy for constructing covalent organic polymers (COPs) with atomically precise iron‐tetrapyrrole units. By incorporating cycloalkane‐based spacers, we selectively tune the π–d orbital interaction between the Fe 3d orbitals and the tetrapyrrole π‐system. This deliberate electronic modulation optimizes the d‐band center and delocalizes electron density, thereby enhancing the intrinsic activity of the Fe–N 4 sites. The optimized polymer linked by cyclohexane (COP‐CYC) exhibits outstanding alkaline ORR performance, achieving a half‐wave potential of 0.90 V and a high turnover frequency of 0.835 e − site −1 s −1 . When integrated into ampere‐hour‐scale zinc–air batteries, COP‐CYC delivers a peak power density of 2.77 W and a capacity of 4.77 Ah, demonstrating its potential for high‐power, high‐capacity energy storage. This work not only establishes a clear relationship between linker‐modulated π–d orbital hybridization and ORR activity but also provides a generalizable molecular‐design strategy for advanced electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Getting the balance right—Considerations of lithium enrichment for the fusion fuel cycle with a focus on nuclear non-proliferation
papers.abstract_en: Fusion reactors are expected to rely on enriched lithium-6 for tritium breeding, but highly enriched lithium-6 also raises non-proliferation concerns because of its relevance to thermonuclear weapons. Because tritium breeding is intrinsically inefficient, some blanket concepts call for very high lithium-6 enrichments. We assess whether such levels are justified by examining cost, breeder blanket design, and proliferation risk. Taken together, these considerations support keeping most commercial fusion applications below the 60% intermediate-grade boundary proposed in this paper. Distinct enrichment thresholds would strengthen safeguards, material accountancy, and supply-chain monitoring. From a non-proliferation perspective, this would preserve a clearer boundary between civil and more sensitive material, making suspicious enrichment activity easier to identify. Such limits would affect some current tritium-breeding concepts and require reassessment of elements of the current breeding paradigm. More broadly, lithium supply and isotopic enrichment should be treated as governance and regulatory priorities for fusion deployment.

papers.title: From wasteland to wonderland: Releasing resupply potential from urban minerals of electric vehicle batteries and motors in China
Engineering e g ‐Orbital of Octahedral Cobalt Cations via High‐Entropy Design for Superior Li–S Batteries in Spinel Co 3 O 4
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Both excessive and insufficient electron filling in e g orbitals of the octahedral cations in spinel transition‐metal oxides, weaken interactions with lithium polysulfide (LiPS) intermediates, thereby impairing their catalytic performance. Herein, we propose a high‐entropy‐driven e g ‐orbital engineering strategy to precisely tune the spin state of octahedral Co cations (Co Oh 3+ ) within the spinel‑type Co 3 O 4 framework. Specifically, partial substitution of Co with multiple metals yields high‑entropy (FeNiMnZn) x Co 3 − x O 4 (HS‑HEOs) catalysts with optimized e g ‐orbital occupancy, thereby promoting strong LiPS adsorption and high catalytic activity. The high‑spin state of Co Oh 3+ and the optimized e g ‐orbital occupancy in HS‑HEOs are jointly regulated through two synergistic mechanisms: intra‐atomic transition from low‐energy t 2g to high‐energy e g orbitals, and interatomic electron transfer mediated by strong Co Oh 3+ ─O─TM quantum spin‑exchange interactions. Concurrently, the high‑spin configuration (t 2g 5 e g 1.65 ) shifts the d ‑band center of Co Oh 3+ upward, which weakens Co Oh 3+ ─O covalency, enhances the polarity of the Co Oh 3+ ─O bonds, and strengthens the chemical affinity for LiPSs, thereby accelerating their conversion kinetics. Consequently, the HS‑HEO‑based cell delivers 963.9 mAh g −1 at 9 C and retains a capacity decay rate of only 0.045% per cycle over 700 cycles at 1 C. This approach opens new pathways for rational design of high‐performance catalysts and holds promise for advancing renewable energy technologies.

papers.title: Engineering Cu 4 Mo 6 Se 8 /Ti 3 C 2 Hetero‐Interfaces to Boost Magnesium Storage Kinetics of Bimetallic MOF‐Derived Selenide Cathode Material for Multilayer Magnesium Metal Pouch Cell
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Conversion‐type selenide cathode materials have shown significant promise for magnesium metal batteries owing to their high theoretical capacity and “soft” lattice characteristics. However, conventional conversion‐type selenide cathodes still suffer from large volume changes, limited bulk‐phase utilization and polyselenide shuttling, leading to unsatisfactory magnesium storage capacity and cycling stability. Here, we construct a MOF‐derived Cu 4 Mo 6 Se 8 /Ti 3 C 2 (CMSe/Ti 3 C 2 ) cathode material with hetero‐interfaces. The hetero‐interface engineering effectively enhances the electronic conductivity and structural stability of CMSe while anchoring polyselenides during cycling. Meanwhile, the introduced 2D Ti 3 C 2 builds a continuous conductive network, synergistically improving charge transport, Mg 2+ diffusion, and bulk‐phase reaction participation. Benefiting from these effects, CMSe/Ti 3 C 2 delivers a high magnesium storage capacity of 215 mAh g −1 at 20 mA g −1 and retains 92% of its capacity over 1500 cycles at 500 mA g −1 . The reversible capacity increases from 54.5 mAh g −1 for CMSe to 122.1 mAh g −1 for CMSe/Ti 3 C 2 . Moreover, the assembled multilayer magnesium metal pouch cell achieves the highest capacity of 75 mAh. The magnesium storage mechanism of CMSe/Ti 3 C 2 based on conversion reactions is investigated through theoretical calculations and advanced characterization techniques. This work provides a new strategy for regulating the phase‐transition behavior and reversibility of conversion‐type selenide cathodes through hetero‐interface engineering.

papers.title: Enantiopurity-Controlled Magnetism in a Two-Dimensional Organic–Inorganic Material
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Extended solids that combine unpaired electron spin and structural chirality can host unconventional magnetic behaviors with potential for electronic technologies. A versatile strategy for creating chiral solids is incorporation of chiral organic molecules into inorganic crystals. However, such hybrid organic–inorganic materials have so far been examined through the lens of absolute chirality, leaving enantiomeric excess ( ee ) underexplored as a tuning parameter. Here, we report two-dimensional (2D) intercalation compounds with controllable ee produced by cation exchange of MnPS 3 with chiral organic molecules. We show that these materials’ magnetism is determined by intercalant ee rather than absolute chirality. Moreover, low- ee materials display thermally activated dynamic magnetism absent from enantiopure analogs. These ee -dependent magnetic behaviors are explained by local ordering of Mn vacancies, directed by correlated vacancy–intercalant electrostatics and confined molecular packing. Together, these results demonstrate a distinctive tuning strategy for molecule–material hybrids and establish design principles for 2D chiral and magnetically dynamic materials.

papers.title: Electronic modulation of rare earth metal gadolinium (Gd) single atom catalysts kinetically boosts bidirectional sulfur redox in lithium sulfur batteries
Electrochemical Activation–Driven Micropore Expansion Toward High–Capacity Hard Carbon Anodes for Advanced Li–Ion Batteries (Adv. Funct. Mater. 61/2026)
Electrically Reconfigurable Phase Change Gly/Hydrogel for Solar‐Thermal Battery
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Phase change materials (PCMs) offer great promise for sustainable thermal energy storage, yet their practical deployment is hindered by unstable supercooling, inefficient solar harvesting, and lack of on‐demand energy release. Here, we propose a novel solar‐thermal battery using an electrically reconfigurable rigid‐flexible switchable phase change gly/hydrogel (PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel) for ultra‐high solar harvesting and long‐term energy storage. The PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel achieves unprecedented metastability down to −30°C with a supercooling degree of up to 88°C due to the H‐bonded solvation network of glycerol, enabling long‐term energy storage without accidental crystallization. Crucially, we develop a novel electrically reconfigurable crystallization technique, enabling on‐demand energy release of the supercooled PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel to realize smart thermal management. Moreover, the PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel also exhibits exceptional photothermal conversion efficiency over the full solar spectrum due to the non‐radiative relaxation of carbon quantum dots (CQDs). Importantly, the strong hydrogen bounding network endowed PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel with excellent water retention and reabsorption capability. These attributes, supported by a robust hydrogen‐bonding network and non‐radiative photothermal mechanisms, make our PAM/SAT‐CQD gly/hydrogel ideal for applications in solar‐thermal battery, as well as wearable thermal management and intelligent thermal regulation systems, offering a scalable solution for renewable energy integration.

papers.title: Efficient battery electrolyte design for electric aircraft driven by physics-augmented AI
Dual‐Strategy Electron Injection Stabilizing High‐Content 1T‐Phase MoS 2 With Sulfur Vacancies for Superior Sodium Storage
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT 1T phase MoS 2 with metallic properties holds great promise as an anode for sodium‐ion batteries owing to its high electrical conductivity. However, the inherent thermodynamic instability of 1T‐MoS 2 poses a significant challenge in achieving stable phases with high content. Herein, we report a facile dual‐strategy electron injection via C 2 O 4 2− intercalation and W‐doping to construct 1T‐rich MoS 2 with sulfur vacancy (W‐C 2 O 4 2− ‐MoS 2‐x ) for enhanced sodium storage. Notably, the synergistic electron injection from C 2 O 4 2− and W not only drives the phase transition from 2H to 1T but also substantially increases the yield of the 1T phase. In addition, the sulfur vacancies generated by W‐doping further reduce the energy barrier for phase transformation. DFT calculations indicate that the co‐incorporation of W and C 2 O 4 2− injects more electrons to MoS 2 , increasing the energy difference for the reverse 1T‐to‐2H transition, thereby favoring the 1T phase stabilization. Consequently, W‐C 2 O 4 2− ‐MoS 2‐x with a high 1T phase content of 74.6% delivers a high reversible capacity of 524.6 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 A g − 1 , excellent rate capability (395.5 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1 ), and outstanding long‐term cycling stability (412.8 mAh g − 1 at 2 A g − 1 after 1000 cycles). This dual‐strategy electron injection provides a new avenue for designing high‐performance MoS 2 anodes.

papers.title: Direct oxygen incorporation to trigger a Li2O-rich solid interphase for uniform lithium deposition
Direct Regeneration of High‐Nickel Cathodes: Overcoming Rock‐Salt Barrier via Li 2 MoO 4 ‐Induced Surface Reconstruction
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Owing to its economic and environmental benefits, direct regeneration has been regarded as a promising approach. However, for degraded high‐nickel layered cathodes during cycling, the rock‐salt phase could be formed on the surface, serving as Li‐ions diffusion barrier, which would inhibit the in‐depth relithiation and structural recovery. Herein, the Li 2 MoO 4 ‐induced surface reconstruction strategy is proposed to successfully regenerate spent NCM. Significantly, the surface properties are further reconstructed, along with the doping of Mo‐atoms into the lattice framework with improved stability. Assisted by ex/in situ exploring, it could be confirmed that Li 2 MoO 4 could promote charge redistribution and strengthen TM─O─Mo coupling, which contributes to the lowering of Li + migration barrier and the recovery of layered phase. As a result, the as‐regenerated NCM delivers a high discharge capacity of 179.1 mAh g − 1 at 1.0 C and retains 87.71% capacity after 200 cycles, better than that of traditional solid‐state regenerated NCM (58.11%). Moreover, the reconstructed surface is beneficial for suppressing structural strain and interfacial side reactions, leading to improved kinetic behavior and stability. This work is expected to shed light on the transformation behaviors for overcoming surface structural barriers, meanwhile offering significant strategies for direct regeneration of high‐nickel cathodes.
papers.summary_ko: Li2MoO4 기반 표면 재구성을 통해 열화된 고니켈 캐소드(NCM)의 록솔트상 장벽을 극복하는 직접 재생 전략을 제시한 연구입니다. Mo 도핑을 통해 전하 재분배를 촉진하고 Li+ 이동 장벽을 낮춰 층상 구조 회복을 유도했습니다.

papers.title: Designing zero-degradation LFP batteries via rational lithium release from LFO additives
Designing and mapping cascade catalysis pathway for balanced polysulfide conversion in Li-S batteries
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Lithium–sulfur batteries are fundamentally constrained by the sluggish 16-electron sulfur reduction reaction. Electrocatalytic sulfur reduction reaction is inherently complex, involving multiple lithium polysulfide intermediates (Li 2 S n , n = 2–8), each with distinct adsorption and activation requirements, leading to unbalanced polysulfide conversion and severe shuttle effect. Although cascade catalysis has been proposed as a potential solution, the precise pathway and its mechanistic role in regulating polysulfide conversion remain elusive. Here we elucidate and experimentally validate the complete cascade pathway of sulfur reduction on Fe,N,S-codoped holey graphene as a model catalyst. Density functional theory reveals that Fe sites preferentially bind and activate long-chain polysulfides, while N,S-C sites accelerate the conversion of Li 2 S 4 to Li 2 S 2 /Li 2 S. Such site-specific synergy balances sulfur reduction kinetics and suppresses polysulfide accumulation. Combined kinetic analysis and operando Raman spectroscopy directly reveal how synergistic cascade catalysis governs the reaction pathway, modulates key intermediates, and enables balanced polysulfide conversion. Together, these results establish cascade catalysis as a mechanism-driven design strategy for lithium–sulfur battery electrodes, where regulation of the reaction pathway suppresses polysulfide shuttling and enables enhanced cycling stability.

papers.title: Dendrite initiation and deflection in biaxially stressed solid electrolytes
Crown‐Shell‐Core Synergistic Ion‐Conduction Strategy via Tailored Solvation Structure for Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Battery
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Designing functional fillers with more accessible Lewis acid sites to regulate the solvation structure is key to developing high‐performance polyethylene oxide (PEO) solid electrolytes, while the enlarged filler/matrix interfaces inevitably lead to compromised Li + transport kinetics. Herein, a “crown‐shell‐core” multi‐dimensional synergistic ion‐conduction strategy of PEO‐based solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) is designed to regulate solvation structure and improve the interfacial compatibility of filler/matrix, which is induced by ionic‐liquid (Li‐IL) impregnated bimetallic UIO‐66(Zr/Hf) (BUIO) (Li‐IL@BUIO, denoted as BUIL) filler. The introduction of structural defects generates abundant open metal sites, serving as Lewis acidic “crowns” capable of immobilizing anions and weakening EO‐Li coordination. The filler with a 3D open framework acts as a host, while the ionic liquid is encapsulated into the pores, forming nanowetted interfaces and rapid Li + transport channels within the core. The PEO‐Li‐IL@BUIO/Cellulose (PIBU/CL) exhibits a high Li + transference number (0.682), high Li + conductivity (5.83 × 10 −4 S cm −1 , 30°C), and a wide electrochemical window up to 4.9 V. The PIBU/CL also demonstrates excellent compatibility and long‐term stability with lithium metal. Impressively, the LFP | PIBU/CL | Li cells deliver an extended cycling life of over 800 cycles at 0.5 C with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%.
papers.summary_ko: 이온성액체가 함침된 이금속 UIO-66(Zr/Hf) 필러(Li-IL@BUIO)를 이용해 PEO 기반 고체전해질의 용매화 구조를 조절하는 '크라운-쉘-코어' 다차원 이온전도 전략을 제시했다. 필러의 개방금속 자리가 루이스 산성 '크라운'으로 작용해 음이온을 고정하고 EO-Li 배위를 약화시켜, 필러/매트릭스 계면 적합성을 높이면서 덴드라이트 없는 리튬 금속 전지를 구현했다.

papers.title: Co‐Assembled Hybrid Interlayer Engineering for Enhanced Upper Interface Stability in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Engineering electron transport layer (ETL) interface is critical for high‐efficiency and long‐term stability in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet co‐assembled hybrid interlayer are rarely explored for this upper interface. This work integrates 4‐aminobenzoate acid hydrochloride (4AA) with a dibenzo‐18‐crown‐6 (DB18C6) to construct a hybrid interlayer at ETL interface. The 4AA molecules intercalate into DB18C6 aggregates, homogenizing the monolayer and boosting surface coverage (from 0.57 to 0.79) and strengthening the interfacial dipole moment (from 2 to 7 Debye). This interlayer provides dual passivation, in which the ─NH 3 + and ─COOH groups of 4AA neutralize ionic defects, while DB18C6 optimizes perovskite crystallinity and energy level alignment. Therefore, modified devices achieve an efficiency of 26.33% (exceeding 22.92% of the control) with high open‐circuit voltage (V OC ) of 1.167 V and fill factor (FF) of 86.05% (compared to 1.130 V and 80.38% of the control). More importantly, the co‐assembled hybrid interlayer serves as a barrier against environmental and ionic degradation. The unencapsulated device demonstrates outstanding operational stability, retaining 93.2% of initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. This work demonstrates a co‐assembly strategy to address efficiency and stability challenges at ETL interface, paving a reliable path toward high‐performance and stable inverted PSCs.

papers.title: Catalyst‐Mediated Interfacial Prelithiation for Energy/Power‐Dense and Ultralong‐Life Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The irreversible cation depletion and interfacial degradation fundamentally limit the practical energy output and cycling endurance of lithium‐free anode batteries. Here, we propose a catalyst‐mediated interfacial prelithiation strategy that offsets irreversible lithium loss, precisely optimizes Li + kinetics and interfacial stability for energy/power‐dense cell prototypes. The sulfurized polyacrylonitrile (SPAN) catalyst, featuring electron‐withdrawing sulfur sites, facilitates C‐C bond cleavage through S‐Li interactions. The Li 2 C 2 O 4 @SPAN composite delivers a delithiation voltage of 3.90 V and a highly efficient Li utilization of 99.5%. When paired with the LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode, the prelithiation layer achieves Li + replenishment areal capacities up to 1.1 mAh cm −2 . Furthermore, the bilayer configuration spatially isolates prelithiation agents from the cathode's redox center, alleviating the gas‐induced structural collapse and stress accumulation. Meanwhile, the SPAN‐derived ROSO 3 Li species form a robust cathode interphase with LiF domains, accelerating Li + transport and stabilizing the 4.5 V charging process. Under the lean‐electrolyte condition (1.7 g Ah −1 ) in 1.28 Ah pouch cells, the Cu||NCM811‐LS prototype achieves gravimetric/volumetric energy densities of 460 Wh kg −1 /1083 Wh L −1 and a peak power output of 858 W kg −1 . In addition, a 2.8 Ah Gr||NCM811 cell incorporating this prelithiation reservoir maintains a capacity retention of 88.2% over 1000 cycles. As a “drop‐in” solution requiring no changes to cell assembly, this interfacial prelithiation paradigm aligns with scalable industrial manufacturing, affording a readily adoptable path toward energy/power‐dense lithium batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 촉매 매개 계면 예비리튬화 전략으로 무음극(리튬 결핍) 전지의 비가역적 양이온 손실과 계면 열화를 상쇄했다. 전자흡인 황 자리를 가진 SPAN 촉매가 S-Li 상호작용을 통해 C-C 결합 절단을 촉진해 Li2C2O4@SPAN 복합체가 3.90V의 탈리튬화 전압과 99.5%의 높은 리튬 이용률을 달성했으며, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 양극과 결합해 1.1 mAh/cm²의 리튬 보충 용량을 구현했다.

papers.title: Breaking Rate‐Limit of Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 by Quasi‐ALD Derived Ultra‐Low Carbon Coating in High‐Rate Sodium‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Carbon coating is a key strategy to enhance electron transport for polyanionic cathode materials. However, current carbon‐coating methods face challenges in simultaneously achieving ultrathin, continuous, and highly conductive coatings with low carbon content, to enable efficient coupled ion–electron transport. As for Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP), it still suffers from the above issues, limiting its electrochemical performance and industrial application. Commercial atomic layer deposition (ALD) technology is highly precise but unsuitable for carbon coatings and requires costly specialized equipment. Here, a precursor‐induced quasi‐ALD carbon deposition strategy is proposed to fabricate high‐power, stable NFPP@C‐FAC cathodes, using molecular‐level coupling of Fe and C sources. The obtained carbon matrix exhibits an ultrathin, uniform coating with an ultra‐low carbon content of 1.5% and few defects. These properties increase the electronic conductivity and the interfacial Na + diffusion kinetics, thereby improving the coupled ion–electron transport, as confirmed by DFT calculations. NFPP@C‐FAC demonstrates excellent rate performance (58 mAh g −1 at 200 C) and exceptional cycling stability, with 83.2% capacity retention after 20 000 cycles at 20 C. Moreover, NFPP@C‐FAC exhibits superior performance over a wide temperature range, which shows 90% capacity retention at −20°C compared to room temperature, with a single‐phase solid‐solution reaction mechanism confirmed by in situ XRD.

papers.title: Bonding-solvation coupling mechanism toward high-performance flexible zinc-iodine batteries
Bioinspired Solvation‐Interfacial Dual Regulation for Subzero‐Tolerant and Long‐Cycling Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) hold great promise for large‐scale green energy storage but suffer from Zn‐metal instability caused by dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, and corrosion. In this work, we introduce inosine (Ino), a natural biomolecule, as an electrolyte additive to address these challenges by leveraging its dual functions of Zn 2+ chelation and Zn‐metal adsorption. Ino effectively replaces water molecules within Zn 2+ solvation sheaths through strong coordination bonds and disrupts the hydrogen‐bonding network among water molecules, thereby reducing free water activity. Simultaneously, Ino preferentially adsorbs onto Zn metal, constructing a stable interfacial layer that guides uniform Zn 2+ deposition. As a result, Zn//Zn symmetric cells exhibit exceptional cycling stability (3300 h) and durability at low temperature (1500 h). Zn//Cu half‐cells achieve a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.07% over 1000 cycles. Full‐cells paired with NH 4 V 4 O 10 (NVO) cathodes retain 77.9% capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Furthermore, a Zn//NVO pouch cell with a low negative/positive capacity (N/P) ratio (3.53) retains 79.1% of its initial capacity after 290 cycles. A more practical pouch cell delivers an initial capacity of 61.14 mAh and maintains stable operation for 100 cycles, underscoring its real‐world viability. This biomolecule‐derived solvation‐interfacial dual‐regulation strategy provides a novel approach for designing eco‐friendly, high‐performance AZMBs.

papers.title: Binder Mitigating Current Collector Corrosion toward 5 V‐Class Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Even with native aluminum oxide (Al 2 O 3 ) passive film, the aluminum (Al) current collector is susceptible to pitting corrosion and anodic dissolution under high voltage (>4.0 V vs. Li + /Li). Herein, a corrosion‐inhibiting binder (named as CSAP) with an ion‐hydrogen bond synergistic network is developed for 5 V‐class LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 (LNMO) batteries, the abundant carboxylate (─COO − ) on the backbone plays a key role in coordinating with Al 2 O 3 , resulting in a stable organic–inorganic hybrid interphase that effectively resists the attack of corrosive species generated from lithium salt. Minor current response is exhibited from the CSAP‐treated Al current collector compared with the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) counterpart during 36 h chronoamperometry test, directly indicating the suppressed corrosion reactions. A similar conclusion can be arrived at from the lower content of corrosion mass loss in finite element analysis. Furthermore, the suppression of transition‐metal ion dissolution endowed by CSAP is verified through the structural retention observed in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Benefiting from these merits, a discharge capacity of 139.4 mAh g −1 is maintained in the LNMO/CSAP battery after 600 cycles at 1 C, compare with 109.7 mAh g −1 of the PVDF counterpart. More encouragingly, a discharge capacity of 108.1 mAh g −1 is exhibited for the LNMO/CSAP battery at 12 C.
papers.summary_ko: 5V급 LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4(LNMO) 리튬 금속 전지에서 알루미늄 집전체의 피팅 부식과 양극 용해를 억제하는 부식방지 바인더(CSAP)를 개발했다. 카복실레이트기가 Al2O3와 배위 결합해 안정적인 유무기 하이브리드 계면상을 형성하며, PVDF 대비 36시간 정전류 시험에서 부식 반응이 억제됨을 직접 확인했다.

papers.title: Asymmetric Ionic Liquid Modulated Anion‐Reinforced Electric Double Layer for Advanced Durable Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The electric double layer (EDL) governs local electrolyte enrichment and reduction pathways, thereby directing the nucleation and evolution of solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, electrolyte design is still largely guided by bulk solvation descriptors. Here, an asymmetric room temperature phosphonium ionic liquid, (2‐methoxyethoxy)methyl phosphonium hexafluorophosphate (PMEP), is designed to promote an anion‐reinforced EDL. Molecular asymmetry lowers the melting point of PMEP and promotes PF 6 − participation in Li + ‐centered solvation structures. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that PF 6 − can participate in Li + ‐centered interfacial solvation clusters under selected charge states, which contributes to the formation of an SEI containing both organic reduction products and inorganic species such as LiF and Li 2 O. This organic/inorganic SEI structure lowers interfacial impedance and the apparent activation barrier for Li + transfer, enabling more uniform lithium deposition and a mechanically robust interface. Li|LiFePO 4 batteries with an areal loading of 11.3 mg cm −2 deliver 94.9% capacity retention after 600 cycles. The fabricated 1.6 Ah Graphite|LiFePO 4 cylindrical cell operates stably for over 500 cycles with a Coulombic efficiency above 99.8%. This work demonstrates a shift in electrolyte design from bulk formulations toward interfacial solvation structure engineering for next generation batteries.

papers.title: An open access solid-state battery cell database to advance visualization, search, analysis, and AI data extraction
papers.abstract_en: Despite thousands of annual publications on battery devices, standard reporting practices are distinctly absent, resulting in a patchwork of reported data that is difficult to analyze. To address this, we constructed a database of research-level solid-state batteries with an ontology-informed data framework reflected in 167 columns and populated with 245 batteries, resulting in over 40,000 data points. This project's significance is 3-fold: (1) our variables include materials, components, fabrication, and cell testing, whose combination is essential to describe and properly assess a solid-state battery. (2) Our inclusion of "not applicable" and "not reported" values enables analysis of reporting practices and insights on "missing data" in battery publications. (3) We present a structure for battery data with well-defined variables, facilitating formatted reporting. Key applications discussed include advanced search workflow employing numerical and categorical criteria for experiment design, streamlined visualization for various actors and utilizations, and a training set for artificial intelligence (AI) paper-data extraction.

papers.title: An interpretable adaptive framework for cross-domain state of health prediction in lithium-ion batteries
Academic battery passports for the regulatory era of energy storage
A dilute nitrate electrolyte for all-climate batteries
A Plant Photoregulator‐Inspired S‐Type Heterojunction System for Diabetic Keratopathy via Tri‐Modal Light‐Driven Immunometabolic Reprogramming, Tissue Repair, and Antibacterial Activity
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Diabetic keratopathy (DK) is a prevalent ocular surface complication of diabetes, frequently unnoticed until significant structural and functional deterioration occurs. Chronic hyperglycemic stress promotes inflammation in the corneal epithelial‐neural‐immune (epineuroimmune) unit, impeding tissue recovery and increasing infection susceptibility. To address this metabolic–immune–infection imbalance, we developed a light‐regulated biomimetic catalytic platform (WCN x ‐Rh2) that integrates glucose degradation and monitoring, immune‐modulated epithelial‐neural regeneration, and antibacterial defense. This platform features an S‐scheme heterojunction (WCN x ) composed of graphitic carbon nitride and tungsten oxide, enabling visible‐light (VIS)‐driven glucose degradation, dark‐state colorimetric detection, and near‐infrared (NIR) photothermal antibacterial activity. Complementarily, the loaded ginsenoside Rh2—identified via systematic screening—inhibits the Nucleotide‐binding and oligomerization domain (NOD)‐like receptor signaling pathway. The combined action of WCN x and Rh2 reduces advanced glycation end products (AGEs), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and inflammatory signaling, reprogramming dendritic cell function to restore epineuroimmune homeostasis and drive tissue repair. These functions were validated in two animal models. In diabetic mice, VIS‐irradiated WCN x ‐Rh2 accelerated corneal epithelial and nerve recovery. In a diabetic keratitis model, NIR‐activated WCN x ‐Rh2 enabled effective corneal bacterial eradication and tissue repair. Overall, this work establishes a light‐driven metabolic‐modulation biomimetic paradigm and proposes an integrated strategy for managing DK.

papers.title: A Novel Na 2 Fe 2 P 2 O 7 SO 4 Cathode Material: Study on the Mechanism of Double Anion Synergistic Coupling and Electrochemical Performance Enhancement
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Polyanionic ca–thode systems offer long cycle life and tunable redox potential due to their three–dimensional rigid skeleton. Here, we design a new Na 2 Fe 2 P 2 O 7 SO 4 cathode with a sulfate–pyrophosphate double anion for the first time. [SO 4 ] 2− and [P 2 O 7 ] 4− tetrahedra are coupled into the FeO 6 /FeO 4 polyhedral skeleton, and in situ biomass carbon coating constructs a highly conductive network with continuous 3D Na + migration channels. Using density functional theory and the climbing–image–driven elastic band method, the effects of different anion compositions on structural stability and sodium ion diffusion are evaluated. Our findings reveal that the composite anion displays the lowest migration energy barrier, thereby confirming the efficacy of the dual–anion synergy strategy in optimizing diffusion kinetics. The resulting Na 2 Fe 2 P 2 O 7 SO 4 /C–BM–2 delivers an initial discharge capacity of 124.70 mAh g −1 (0.05 C), a reversible capacity of 88.15 mAh g −1 at 1 C, and retains 64.43% after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. At −25°C, capacity retention reaches 95.46% after 1000 cycles at 0.5 C. This dual–anion–regulated material provides an innovative design for high‐energy, wide–temperature, long–life polyanion cathodes, particularly suitable for large–scale energy storage sodium–ion batteries requiring safety and durability.

papers.title: A NIR‐II Excitable Hyperbranched Conjugated Polymer‐Based Phototheranostic for Enhanced Tumor Radioimmunotherapy via Synergistic Cuproptosis and STING Activation
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Radioresistance and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (ITME) present formidable challenges in cancer radioimmunotherapy. Herein, we report a multifunctional nanotheranostic platform ( 1 2 5 I/Cu/BCP@HA) that integrates radiotherapy with delivery of copper ions, aiming to induce cuproptosis and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) release to amplify cGAS‐STING pathway activation. The 1 2 5 I/Cu/BCP@HA is constructed from an NIR‐II‐excitable hyperbranched conjugated polymer that is co‐assembled with 1 2 5 I and Cu 2 O via tyrosine coordination. Upon dual stimulation by the acidic TME and NIR‐II laser irradiation, the platform responsively releases copper ions and 1 2 5 I. The liberated copper ions deplete intracellular glutathione, catalyze hydroxyl radical generation, and trigger mitochondrial dysfunction, culminating in cuproptosis accompanied by mtDNA release. Concurrently, the platform exerts potent radiosensitizing effects, further amplifying the sustained nuclear DNA (nucDNA) damage induced by 1 2 5 I. The combined release of mtDNA and nucDNA fragments synergistically activates the cGAS‐STING pathway, promoting type I interferon secretion and immunogenic cell death (ICD). This coordinated response facilitates dendritic cell maturation, augments CD4 + /CD8 + T cell infiltration, and reverses TME immunosuppression, demonstrating robust antitumor efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes a novel nanotheranostic strategy that synergistically integrates radiotherapy, photothermal therapy, cuproptosis, and STING pathway activation for enhanced cancer radioimmunotherapy.

papers.title: A Mechanistic Study of Bio‐Based Nanotemplated Carbon Nanofibers Derived From Water Processable Lignin Blends for Sustainable Energy Storage Applications (Adv. Mater. 39/2026)
papers.abstract_en: Bio-Based Nanotemplated Carbon Nanofibers In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.72508), Maurice N. Collins, Tadhg Kennedy, Mario Culebras, and co-workers demonstrate a fully water based electrospinning route to sustainable carbon nanofibers using lignosulfonate, gelatin, and alginate—eliminating organic solvents and synthetic binders. Gelatin and alginate act as sacrificial templates to create engineered hollow nanostructures. A mechanistic study links carbon hybridization to electrochemical behavior, and the resulting carbons are evaluated for sodium ion battery applications.
